testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with one foot on the accelerator and one foot on the brake.
Leave the road safely and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road safely and stop.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning light comes on, you must stop the vehicle while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In a vehicle with one air brake system, the pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within three minutes after the engine reaches operating speed.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the air tanks?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, what does it mean?

options.text: The ABS cannot work because of weather.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: The ABS warning light means something in the anti-lock braking system is not working correctly.

questions.question: What does the air compressor do in a truck with air brakes?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol to the system?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To keep people from breathing the air.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to help stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What is the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half force.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer, release the brakes, turn the wheel, then press the brakes again.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tanks completely.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks from too much pressure. It normally opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: Emergency brakes:

options.text: Are not required on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, once air pressure is lost and the spring brakes come on:

options.text: You will be unable to move the vehicle.
A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use the spring brakes to drive normally.
The air tanks will automatically refill to a safe pressure level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the proper control releases the spring brakes briefly, allowing you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.

questions.question: In cold weather, an alcohol evaporator should be checked and filled:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator helps prevent ice buildup in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used:

options.text: To make the air brakes work better.
To temporarily release the spring brakes.
To charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To temporarily release the spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with dual parking control valves have a separate air tank. This tank can temporarily release the spring brakes if they activate due to low air pressure. Pushing the proper control releases the spring brakes briefly, allowing you to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: A wig wag is:

options.text: A tube that carries air to the brakes.
A type of air brake system.

questions.explanation: Air brake vehicles must have a low pressure warning device. A wig wag is one type. When air pressure drops to 55-75 psi, a mechanical arm drops into your view.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system is very low on pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work at all.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There will be no noticeable effect.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system gets very low on pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop the vehicle safely and have the air system repaired.

questions.question: On trucks and buses, where are ABS malfunction lamps located?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle by the passenger's door

questions.explanation: Trucks, tractors, and buses with anti-lock brakes have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.

questions.question: Air pressure should build up in a single air system within:
questions.explanation: In single air systems, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi within three minutes.

questions.question: If braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag can add ____ to your vehicle's total stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to total stopping distance.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking action.
Hold enough air for several braking actions even if the compressor stops working.
Hold air only during an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking actions even if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks store compressed air for braking. They hold enough air to let the brakes work several times if the compressor fails.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: Hold air for only one braking action.
Hold enough air for several braking actions even if the compressor stops working.
Hold air only during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking actions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking actions even if the compressor stops working.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: When can brakes go out of adjustment?
questions.explanation: Brakes can quickly go out of adjustment if they overheat from heavy use. You should check brake adjustment often.

questions.question: What is the purpose of ABS?

options.text: Stop the air compressor from getting too hot.
Stop the front brakes from working on ice.
Stop the brakes from being used if downshifting would work better.

questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What type of brake system do most heavy trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks use dual air brake systems. This means two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.
